title: How autobuild has failed, so it does not fail the same way again
summary: Each item happened. (1) v0.5 passed its own tests, was published by autobuild, then could not start: its tests never started the service entry point. (2) v0.3 to v0.5 integrated only the newest ZIP of a batch, silently dropping the rest. (3) Wrapped ZIPs (one top folder) were rejected. (4) Packages declared a publish source that only their tests create. (5) Execute bits are lost in ZIP extraction. (6) A runner printed PASS, then ran an unconfigured test that exited 2. (7) Work was never submitted at all.
invariants: An autobuild change must include a test that starts the real service entry point (v0.5.1 tests/test_end_to_end.py does).
A silent service is a failed service: check --status and the receipts, not the absence of errors.
Work that is not in Git does not exist for the next chat: commit it, even unqualified, and say so.

provenance.claim: Batch downloads lost all but the newest ZIP.
The mutation test now gets its database before PASS is printed.
Declared publish sources that only tests generate.
